title: CHARACTER & INTEGRITY: THE HIDDEN STRENGTH BEHIND WISDOM

sense.text:
“For froward thoughts separate from God.” This is where we fall off the horse: you have your own mind. A froward thought is your worldly thought, and it separates you from God because you are not on the same playing field the Lord has you on. You want to do what you want to do, not what the Lord is telling you to do.

You think you know better than the Lord. You think you know better than the men that are over you, the men that rule over you. That means your mind is not on the Lord at all; you have separated yourself by your own thoughts, because you are doing your own damn thing. And that means, ultimately, you lack character. You lack integrity.

Froward thoughts separate from God, “and his power, when it is tried, reproveth the unwise.”

This is a fix-your-spirit class, and we all have to fix our spirit, because Satan is coming. When we thought we were good, we still had a long way to go. People are going to be put in compromising positions where they have to use integrity and good character to get out of it, so we have to tighten up our spirit and keep building it.

“For into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter.” Wisdom cannot enter somebody with a malicious soul: a person that cannot be corrected, a person without good moral character, whose mind is not on what the Lord’s mind is on. Wisdom cannot stay there.

That is why some brothers are perceptive cons. They know all the scriptures, but they cannot keep rank and they are always having issues. You know all these scriptures; why are you not applying them? Because of bad judgment and bad moral character.

“For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding, and will not abide when unrighteousness cometh in.” When you have discipline, the holy spirit of discipline flees deceit, and it will not stay where unrighteousness comes in.

“Therefore he that speaketh unrighteous things cannot be hid: neither shall vengeance, when it punisheth, pass by him.” You speak unrighteousness, and eventually it is going to come out. When you lack character and integrity and do something you know is wrong, those things are going to come out. There is no getting around it.

Sometimes things come out and we do not even know how the Lord brought them out, but they came out when they were supposed to. That brother was not going to say anything. That sister was going to maintain her innocence the whole time, while she was out doing wickedness on the job, in the parking lot, where she thought nobody in the congregation could see her. You did not think we would find out? These things happen in Israel, brothers and sisters doing wild things, and how they get found out is wild: somebody sees them in a store or in a car with somebody, and it all comes out. The Lord will reveal it.

When Moses died, the mantle passed to Joshua, and the men followed the leader, with everybody else behind them. We have to have that spirit. When Joshua finished speaking to them, “they answered Joshua, saying, All that thou commandest us we will do, and whithersoever thou sendest us, we will go.”

Certain things are not going to come straight from the Lord. They are going to come as: I need you to do this, I need you to do that, straighten this up. Wherever they were sent, they would go. That should be our manner.

The complaining spirit and the doubtful spirit come down to this: you do not have faith. You do not believe that the men, the bishops, the deacons, the men over you, are put in place by God. So you are not denying them, you are denying God, because those men were set up by God. That evil spirit of unbelief hinders your understanding.

“According as we hearkened unto Moses in all things, so will we hearken unto thee: only the Lord thy God be with thee, as he was with Moses.” They believed Moses was the man of the Lord.

This shows that Moses led the people with integrity and character, and with Joshua ministering underneath Moses, they saw the same characteristics in him. That is why it was not a hard transition: we are going to follow you just like we followed Moses, whatever you tell us to do we will do, because they saw how he moved. It is the company you keep. Joshua was under Moses, and Caleb did the same thing. These men are examples of a very good moral compass and very good character, and they displayed it because Moses was judging the nation of Israel. When Israel was in their niggerdom in the wilderness, Moses had to keep up his integrity to keep going.

Yet there are elders from other camps, certain unsavory black Hebrew Israelite camps, saying Moses left the truth, that he was off and did not have the spirit. It says right there: “as he was with Moses.” Shame on you for not reading the scriptures, and shame on the men that follow you.

precepts.why:
“Make not thyself an underling to a foolish man.” The camps that say Moses left the truth, when the scripture says the Lord was with him, have made themselves students to a negro that is just as dumb as they are.

The scripture says the Lord was with Joshua “as he was with Moses.” Shame on them for not reading the scriptures, and shame on the men that follow them, because they have made themselves underlings to a foolish man.

sense.text: These are biblical examples of integrity, and Joseph comes first. He was put in a compromising situation, and he paid for it too. He was brought down to Egypt and bought by Potiphar, “an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian.” “And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man.”
“And his master saw that the Lord was with him.” His master saw that this man was different: this man’s God is with him.

“And he left all that he had in Joseph’s hand.” Joseph had control over everything when his master left. “And Joseph was a goodly person, and well favoured.” He had a very good reputation; people looked at him as a man with integrity and good character.
Then “his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.” She looked at this handsome negro who had it all: my husband is not here, I want you and I need you.

“But he refused.” I do not want you; what is wrong with you? You are another man’s wife. He committed everything to my hand, but he did not give me you. He said, “neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife.” This is a man that understands what is going on.

This has happened in Israel: people have committed adultery. You get close to a sister in the truth, you know she is married, and when you are alone bad things happen. These scriptures are here for a reason, and when you uphold them it shows the moral character and the ethics that you have.

Then he said, “how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?” This is wicked as hell. Joseph had integrity. Nobody was watching him. He could have done it, but he said no. This is where integrity comes from: making the right decisions when nobody is watching.

And mind you, these were the nations. They have no moral integrity. They write the laws, the dissertations, the theories and the commentaries, but they lack it themselves and do not know how to implement it.
It came to pass, “as she spake to Joseph day by day, that he hearkened not unto her.” She kept coming to him, day after day, and he would not hearken.

Joseph went into the house to do his business, and “there was none of the men of the house there within. And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled.” Nobody was there this time. Like in the cartoons, she grabbed him and the clothes were left in her hand and he was gone.

He knew she was trying to get him caught up, and he knew this wickedness would destroy everything: his reputation and everything he had worked so hard for. Things would not prosper in his hands anymore if he fell for it. And it would not be her he was sinning against; ultimately he would be sinning against the Lord. This is a very good example of integrity. Read on in Genesis 39: he ended up going to prison behind it, because she lied on him.

precepts.why:
“Sit not at all with another man’s wife”. At all. Do not play with it. Do not sit around another man’s wife; bad things are going to happen if you do. Do not sit with her, “nor sit down with her in thine arms, and spend not thy money with her at the wine.” Do not be buying her drinks; do not be drinking around somebody else’s wife.

Why? “lest thine heart incline unto her.” Negro, you are going to fall for her. She feels her husband is not doing something right, you feel your wife is not doing something right, and two demons coming together is the perfect storm, “and so through thy desire thou fall into destruction.” You are going to fall, and both of you are going to destroy everything.

That is why Joseph called it “this great wickedness”: he would not sit with another man’s wife, and the scripture he upheld shows the moral character he had.

sense.text:
“Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man”. This is a man that had integrity, very good moral character and ethics. The Lord said there was nobody on the earth like him; that was the standard he had.

A man “that feareth God, and escheweth evil? and still he holdeth fast his integrity.” He lost his children. He lost everything he had. He had boils all over his body and could not even sit down. When you have a boil anywhere, you are in agony; your spirit is not right and you do not feel good. It is a recipe for not upholding your integrity, and still he held fast his integrity, “although thou movedst me against him, to destroy him without cause.”

“Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.” Listen how Satan goes into the woman. When things are not right and a woman feels uncomfortable in the situation, Satan tries to infiltrate her. Women like security; they like to be comfortable in the security of the house, and when things are in shambles, Satan is creeping.

What type of thing is this? After everything the Lord has given us, now you tell me to curse God? What is wrong with you, woman? Shut your damn mouth. She wanted to retreat, but when things get rough you have to draw nearer to the Most High, not separate yourself. A woman trying to get her security and her normalcy back says curse God and die; she is not in the spirit. Wicked as hell.

“Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh.” You are a fool; you sound like a heathen. “What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” After all the Lord gave us, you think we are not going to have bad times?

“In all this did not Job sin with his lips.” He did not do what that wicked woman said. He upheld his integrity through trials and tribulations, when things were inconvenient.

Job’s three friends, “Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite”, “made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.” Your friends see what is going on with you: the brother is losing everything, let us go build him up. Now you see the type of men you are around. That is true friendship.

When they saw him, “they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his mantle.” “So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.”

When things are so bad you just are there with him: we are not going to talk about it, I do not even know what to say, I am here with you as your moral support, and whenever you want to talk about it, we will. That is how you know it is us. We just wait for him to say something first, because we do not want to say something out of whack. There is always that one brother who says, to hell with it, and breaks the ice the wrong way and makes it awkward.

precepts.why:
“Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault”, if he is going through something, “ye which are spiritual”, those that surround you, your inner circle, “restore such an one in the spirit of meekness.” You have to build and restore that man back to life, speak life into that brother and get him back on track. Sometimes you are going through burdens that are hard and you do not know how you will get out. You need somebody there for you, not somebody telling you to curse God and die, but somebody saying: get up, bro. Come eat, come to the campfire at the house, and we will go over the scriptures and build you back up.

Restore him, “considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.” If we were in that same situation, we would want our brothers to come and get us out of it. The scriptures are written to build us up and maintain our good character and integrity.

“Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.” That is what Job’s friends were doing when they came to mourn with him. That is loving your neighbor as yourself, on which all the laws hang.

sense.text:
“Then the presidents and princes sought to find occasion against Daniel concerning the kingdom; but they could find none occasion nor fault; forasmuch as he was faithful, neither was there any error or fault found in him.” There was no error or fault in Daniel. This man lived up to the name integrity.

Even when they tried to force them to worship other gods, they said: Nigga, I ain’t doing it. I ain’t going for that. You got to burn us; do whatever you do. And the Lord showed favor to Daniel for it. That is living up to integrity.

Now the terrible examples, of not upholding good character and integrity. “Then saith one of his disciples, Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, which should betray him, Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred pence, and given to the poor?” This is what was happening in Matthew 26.

“This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief.” He was a thief. This man walked with Christ and saw many miracles, and still betrayed the saviour, and betrayed the disciples and everybody else around him. People like that are around, but not really around; they are just taking up space. That is not the type of character you need. This is a person that lacks integrity.

Money was the root and the god of Judas. Greed: he wanted more and more. They were casting out demons and doing miracles. What more do you want?

This is the kind of person the other nations expect you to be: greedy, lacking integrity and morals. This is how they infiltrate organizations, through money. Organizations fail because of money: they come in, offer money, and the organization gives itself up, because it lacked integrity and let money dictate, maneuver and control the movement. That is not happening here. It happened once, with One West. It is not happening again.

precepts.why:
The other nations expect us to be that greedy individual, the one that lacks integrity. At work, your coworkers wonder about you: this brother never murmurs with us, he never works the Sabbath with us.

“Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations.” This is your wisdom and your integrity. So when they sit there wondering why this brother is not greedy, why he moves in such a perfect manner, here is why: “which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.” They say, that brother is a very wise individual; he has integrity. Keeping the statutes is our wisdom, and that is what we give them, instead of the Judas they expect.

sense.text:
King Saul is a very good example of not keeping up integrity and lacking character when it came down to it. He wanted to please men more than he wanted to please God, and the Most High dealt with him.

“I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord, and thy words: because I feared the people.” He chose to disobey the Lord because he feared the people more than he feared the Most High God. That is a problem, and a lot of people deal with it even here. You are worried about pleasing men, but not worried about pleasing the Lord. You cannot do that.

precepts.why:
“Saul said unto him, Blessed be thou of the Lord: I have performed the commandment of the Lord. And Samuel said, What meaneth then this bleating of the sheep in mine ears, and the lowing of the oxen which I hear? And Saul said, They have brought them from the Amalekites: for the people spared the best of the sheep.”

What did the Lord say to do to Amalek? Kill everything, the sheep too. Nothing should have been alive when they left there. But Saul wanted to do his own damn thing: pride, not listening, self-will. That is the transgression he confessed when he said he feared the people.

And what happened? The Lord stopped dealing with Saul, and he started destroying himself, being destroyed mentally over time, lacking integrity and character.

sense.text: “And Saul was very wroth, and the saying displeased him; and he said, They have ascribed unto David ten thousands, and to me they have ascribed but thousands: and what can he have more but the kingdom?” You are the king, and you are jealous? Jealousy and envy are bad character; they are a lack of character.

“And Saul eyed David from that day and forward.” The evil spirit from God came upon him, and “Saul cast the javelin; for he said, I will smite David even to the wall with it.”

By not keeping his integrity and not having good moral character, Saul continued to wax worse. His character declined even more over time. When you do not listen to the Lord, when you try to please other people and not the Lord, you are going to destroy yourself. It is only a matter of time, and it will be open to the public. Everybody saw the decline of Saul.

A person who acts righteous around leadership but differently everywhere else fears men more than he fears God, as Saul did. That is image management, not integrity. Integrity means being consistent everywhere, in any moment; it shows up when things are hard and inconvenient and you still uphold your vows, values, morals and ethics. That integrity is the action behind your character, and it builds your character up.

Paul had this problem with certain brothers and sisters. “Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only.” Some people just show themselves to be that guy in front of everybody. You got them sisters: a brother has a wife, and he knows she ain’t right. She is over there talking about shalom, and she is a damn demon.

Not in my presence only, “but now much more in my absence.” You need to be the same in the absence of everybody. This is the perfect biblical example of integrity: obey in my absence, and “work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.”

“The Lord shall judge the people: judge me, O Lord, according to my righteousness, and according to mine integrity that is in me.” Judge me by my integrity and my righteousness, Lord. Judge me by my actions, by the decisions I make when times are hard. That is our works: we are going to be accounted for our actions and our works in righteousness.

The commandments and the wisdom of the Lord are the foundation of your integrity. When you uphold them, you will have very good integrity, and with it you will build a strong character that people can be proud to be around. You want to be known by the leadership for very good character and integrity, able to make decisions, not for trying to portray something you are not in front of the people while you are sinning against the Lord.

Integrity also means you are not going to get everything right. When you mess up, you say something; that is integrity too. People know the right answer, but their actions choose something completely different, and that is the problem. If you are struggling, brothers, with porn, tell someone; go to someone who has integrity and let them know. Hatred and envy will come out and show themselves, even five years later. Murmuring is a lack of integrity and character, and there is a lot of it in the body. We have to shut that down.

It is easier to look righteous publicly than to change privately. Until you apply what the Bible says, it is just words on the page; you have to believe what you read and put it into action. And when a brother or sister apologizes sincerely after wrongdoing, good character forgives wisely and allows room for repentance and growth. Sincerity is seen over time, but holding on to bitterness years after it was talked out is not right. Let it go.

Wisdom is not proven by how deep you sound, how many scriptures you know, or how spiritual you appear. Wisdom is revealed through consistency, discipline, humility, honesty and integrity. “Therefore we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard, lest at any time we should let them slip.”

Look into yourself and examine whether you have been moving with integrity, or whether you are lacking moral and ethical character. These things matter in your walk: the type of husband, father, leader and mother you are. We have to be around people who are not just yes men and women, but who will challenge your integrity and your character by helping you build them.
